title: A keycard
description: The data an answer rests on: the thresholds a finding is computed under, the attributions a holder asserts, and the terms of events they know about. A card is a citation and not a credential — an API key here would put a secret in a file whose purpose is to be shared. Nothing reads this file at run time: `chainlens.keycard.load` is the enforcement, and its refusals are what a holder meets. This is the declared shape, for a reader and for an editor that offers completion. Every field is optional, because a card states what it states and inherits the rest from the shipped baseline, per item: a card naming one threshold keeps the library's values for the other four, and a card naming one address keeps the shipped assertions about every other address.

schema_version.description: Bumped when the shape of a card changes. The loader refuses a version it does not know rather than guessing at a newer one.

keyholder.description: Who is asserting the right to use these values. Nothing in the library reads it; it is here so that a card found in a directory says whose it is, which is the first question a reader of one asks.

thresholds.description: The numbers a finding is computed under. **Unstated means inherited, not defaulted** — and the difference is what makes an overlay per item possible, so a loader must keep `null` distinct from a stated value.

hedge_tolerance.description: How much wider a hedge word makes an amount's band, as a fraction of the amount. The largest free parameter in the whole calculation: it moves the likelihood ratio roughly linearly, and a reader of a finding is entitled to know which value produced the number in front of them.

min_joint_successes.description: Below this many joint successes, an estimate is not reported at all — a rate from three observations is not a rate.

z_95.description: The normal quantile for a 95% interval.

scan_limit.description: How many of a sender's transactions to walk before declaring the scan truncated. A claim about a busy exchange address is not one this machinery can price, and saying so is better than walking a million transactions to find out that it could have.

transfer_limit.description: How many transfers one finding carries in its evidence. The cap is reported when it is hit: a partial list that looks complete is worse than a short one that says it is short.

labels.description: Attributions the holder asserts. **The card speaks for the addresses it names and not for every other** — the shipped assertions about anything else are kept.

presets.description: Terms of events the holder knows about, in the same shape `presets/records.py::Preset` validates — a citable source, rate tiers that increase. **The same type the shipped data uses**, so a holder's terms are checked by the same rules rather than by a second and weaker set. The shipped presets are *rendered* into `SHIPPED` from `presets/data/*.yaml` by `tools/gen_shipped_data.py`; a card's overlay them per event name. The item schema is deliberately not restated here: the rules live in the model, and a second description of them would be a second place they can disagree.

name.description: The label itself — "Mt Gox", "the July proceeds". Distinct from `kind`, which is the category: "this is an exchange" is what a source says, where the name is what it is called.

kind.description: What kind of real-world actor the address is believed to be. **A category and not an identity**, which is what lets the same address be an exchange in one source and sanctioned in another without either being wrong. See `chainlens.models.enums.EntityKind`. **These members are held to `EntityKind` by a test rather than trusted**: this list was hand-written first and was already missing a member and out of order, which is the defect the vocabulary table exists to prevent one layer down. A schema is a second description of a shape Python owns, and the only safe version of that is one something compares.

source.description: Where the assertion can be read. **Required, and a URL rather than a sentence**, because a label with no citation is an assertion nobody can check — a claim dressed as a finding. This is the whole of the card's citation story: there is deliberately no `verify_status`-style field, because a field that could not be checked by a tool, required anyway, teaches people to fill it in rather than to know the answer.
